title: The Chamber Where Books Dream of Being Read by Rain

features.name: book-tower
features.desc-on-touch: A tower of unbound pages stacked so high they remember when they were separate books. The tower hums—it's waiting for rain that leaks through the chamber walls to find it.

features.name: rain-pool
features.desc-on-touch: A shallow pool where rain collects inside the sealed chamber—impossible, but the archive has learned to collect what should not exist. The water is warm and reads as it rests.

features.name: reading-frame
features.desc-on-touch: A barely-3D apparatus of rod and wire, designed to hold a page at the exact angle where rain can read it. The frame glitches—it keeps adjusting itself for rain that isn't falling yet.

features.name: page-sprites
features.desc-on-touch: Small creatures of paper and ink, learning to move like water. They scatter when you're not watching, gathering where rain is about to fall, as if they remember thirst.

features.name: archive-heart
features.desc-on-touch: A circuit board at the chamber's center, sealing the archive's first understanding: that to keep something is to let it be read by forces you cannot control. The chip blooms with soft light when rain reaches it.

features.name: rain-gauge
features.desc-on-touch: A plaque etched with marks for rain-depth, measured in readings instead of inches. The scale reads: 0 (unread), 1 (glimpsed), 2 (known), 3 (understood), and then marks that have no words.

inscription: the pages learned that rain is a reader which understands them—each drop a distinct eye, each storm a perfect reading

file.name: Pages_Rewritten_By_Water_1990_Onward.txt
file.note: Transcripts of pages that altered when exposed to rain—not decay, but rereading. Katita's annotations note that pages seem to remember the rain and write themselves differently the next time it falls

exits.label: upward to pages that learned they couldn't be held
downward into sediment where narrative rests as stone remembering water
westward to the study where books have learned to teach each other
